speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've had episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help you, please tell me when these episodes first started and how long they typically last. Also, do you feel any spinning sensation, or is it more of a lightheaded feeling?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Given your age, the sudden onset of position-dependent vertigo with a sensation of spinning, and absence of other acute neurological or systemic symptoms, the clinical picture strongly suggests BPPV. I will proceed with a targeted physical examination to confirm this.
